correctness.rationale: The four quadratic-character values sum to an integer in [-4,4], so p>3 suffices to transfer the defining-field equation exactly to an integer zero sum. Fourier orthogonality, G^2=chi(-1)q, and exact Laurent coefficient extraction establish both formulas for every prime power; the included checker verifies the resulting Laurent-polynomial identities symbolically and enumerates small prime/extension fields independently. The coordinate-axis uniqueness proof exhausts zero/nonzero possibilities, and the reproduced derivative proof establishes geometric smoothness. No unsupported inference from finite samples is used.

value.rationale: The exact number of rational points on a published smooth blocking curve is its natural quantitative finite-geometric size, absent from the original binary incidence theorem. The closed 3/8-density formulas for infinitely many varying finite fields, split by q mod 4, reveal how costly this construction is as a blocking set and quantify a natural degeneration of axis incidence. This is not a routine substitution of the original blocking theorem, and the proof requires a nontrivial global four-character Gauss-sum evaluation. No broader breakthrough or optimized blocking set is claimed.
